selected_result: Blanchard–Higham–Mary Theorem 4.2: matrix–vector backward error and matrix–matrix forward error when each inner product uses FABsum

bibliographic_source.title: A Class of Fast and Accurate Summation Algorithms

paper_locations.anchor: FABsum block algorithm and lower-level summation backward-error constants
Every matrix-vector or matrix-matrix entry computed by a full FABsum inner product; both labelled theorem conclusions

task_clarification: For all compatible matrix dimensions and a positive block size b dividing the common inner-product length n, compute every entry of y_hat=Ax and C_hat=AB using the actual Algorithm 4.1 FABsum inner product, including rounded products, block FastSum, and AccurateSum.

Formalize both conclusions: y_hat=(A+Delta A)x with entrywise |Delta A| bounded by the appropriate source coefficient times |A|, and entrywise |C_hat-AB| bounded by the same coefficient times |A|*|B|.
Use Theorem 4.1's coefficient u+epsilon_a(n/b)+epsilon_f(b)+O(u^2) or a precise finite-u bound justifying it, with source-equivalent lower-level algorithm/error assumptions.
scope_constraints: Both matrix-vector and matrix-matrix parts of Theorem 4.2 are required; a partial case split is unfaithful.
The matrix-vector conclusion is a structured backward-error statement with a single Delta A, not just a componentwise forward-error inequality.
The matrix-matrix conclusion uses the matrix product |A||B|, not the entrywise absolute value of AB or a norm bound.
Do not postulate either complete conclusion or the complete inner-product bound as a task-local axiom. Source-equivalent FastSum/AccurateSum contracts may be used only below the inner-product layer.
Do not narrow the dimensions, signs, cancellation behavior, block sizes, or source floating-point arithmetic domain.
